title.zh: 卷九十八 志第五十一 禮一
title.raw: 卷九十八 志第五十一 禮一 Volume 98 Treatises 51: Rites 1

sentences.zh: 吉禮一

translations.literal: Auspicious Rites, Part One
translations.idiomatic: Auspicious Rites, Part One

sentences.zh: 五代之衰亂甚矣，其禮文儀注往往多草創，不能備一代之典。

translations.literal: The decline and disorder of the Five Dynasties was extreme; their ritual texts and ceremonial regulations were mostly improvised and could not constitute the full canon of an age.
translations.idiomatic: The decline and disorder of the Five Dynasties was extreme; ritual texts and ceremonial regulations were mostly improvised and could not constitute a full canon for an age.

sentences.zh: 宋太祖興兵間，受周禪，收攬權綱，一以法度振起故弊。

translations.literal: Emperor Taizu of Song, amid military campaigns, received the abdication of Zhou, gathered authority into his hands, and by law and regulation revived long-neglected abuses.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Taizu of Song, amid military campaigns, received the Zhou abdication, gathered authority into his hands, and used law and regulation to revive long-neglected abuses.

sentences.zh: 即位之明年，因太常博士聶崇義上《重集三禮圖》，詔太子詹事尹拙集儒學之士詳定之。

translations.literal: In the year after his accession, because Court of Imperial Sacrifices doctor Nie Chongyi submitted the Recompiled Diagrams of the Three Rites, an edict ordered Grand Mentor of the Heir Apparent Yin Zhuo to gather Confucian scholars to determine them in detail.
translations.idiomatic: In the year after his accession, because Court of Imperial Sacrifices doctor Nie Chongyi submitted the Recompiled Diagrams of the Three Rites, an edict ordered Grand Mentor of the Heir Apparent Yin Zhuo to gather Confucian scholars to review them in detail.

sentences.zh: 開寶中，四方漸平，民稍休息，乃命御史中丞劉溫叟、中書舍人李昉、兵部員外郎、知制誥盧多遜、左司員外郎、知制誥扈蒙、太子詹事楊昭儉、左補闕賈黃中、司勳員外郎和峴、太子中舍陳鄂撰《開寶通禮》二百卷，本唐《開元禮》而損益之。

translations.literal: During Kaibao, as the four quarters gradually settled and the people gained some respite, Censor-in-Chief Liu Wensou, Secretariat Drafter Li Fang, Vice Director of the Ministry of War and Drafting Edict Officer Lu Duoxun, Vice Director of the Left Secretariat Office and Drafting Edict Officer Hu Meng, Grand Mentor of the Heir Apparent Yang Zhaojian, Left Supplementation Aide Jia Huangzhong, Vice Director of the Ministry of Personnel He Xian, and Heir Apparent Attendant Chen E were ordered to compile the Kaibao Comprehensive Rites in two hundred juan, based on the Tang Kaiyuan Rites with additions and subtractions.
translations.idiomatic: During Kaibao, as the empire gradually settled and the people gained some respite, Liu Wensou, Li Fang, Lu Duoxun, Hu Meng, Yang Zhaojian, Jia Huangzhong, He Xian, and Chen E were ordered to compile the Kaibao Comprehensive Rites in two hundred juan, based on the Tang Kaiyuan Rites with additions and subtractions.

sentences.zh: 既又定《通禮義纂》一百卷。

translations.literal: They also fixed the Collected Exegesis of the Comprehensive Rites in one hundred juan.
translations.idiomatic: They also compiled the Collected Exegesis of the Comprehensive Rites in one hundred juan.

sentences.zh: 太宗尚儒雅，勤於治政，修明典章，大抵曠廢舉矣。

translations.literal: Emperor Taizong valued refined learning, was diligent in governing affairs, and clarified statutes and regulations; for the most part, what had long lain neglected was revived.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Taizong prized scholarly refinement, applied himself diligently to government, and restored the ritual codes; on the whole, institutions that had long fallen into disuse were brought back into practice.

sentences.zh: 真宗承重熙之後，契丹既通好，天下無事，於是封泰山，祀汾陰，天書、聖祖崇奉迭興，專置詳定所，命執政、翰林、禮官參領之。

translations.literal: Emperor Zhenzong, after succeeding in the Chongxi era, once the Khitan had made peace and the realm was untroubled, thereupon performed the feng sacrifice on Mount Tai and sacrificed at Fenyin; veneration of the Heavenly Writ and the Sage Ancestor arose in succession, and a special Detailed Determination Office was established, with chief ministers, Hanlin academicians, and ritual officials ordered to take part in directing it.
translations.idiomatic: After Emperor Zhenzong came to the throne in the Chongxi era, peace was made with the Khitan and the empire knew no major disturbances. He then carried out the feng rites on Mount Tai and sacrifices at Fenyin, while cults devoted to the Heavenly Writ and the Sage Ancestor rose one after another. A special office for detailed ritual determination was set up, and chief ministers, Hanlin scholars, and ritual officials were appointed to oversee it jointly.

sentences.zh: 尋改禮儀院，仍歲增修，纖微委曲，緣情稱宜，蓋一時彌文之制也。

translations.literal: Shortly thereafter it was renamed the Court of Ritual Protocol, and year by year revisions were added; minute details were worked out in full, adjusted to circumstances as fitting—altogether the elaborate ritual fashion of that age.
translations.idiomatic: The office was soon renamed the Court of Ritual Protocol and revised year after year. Every minute detail was elaborated and fitted to circumstance—altogether the hyper-formal ritual style of that period.

sentences.zh: 自《通禮》之後，其制度儀注傳於有司者，殆數百篇。

translations.literal: From the time of the Comprehensive Rites onward, the institutions and ceremonial regulations transmitted among the responsible offices amounted to nearly several hundred sections.
translations.idiomatic: After the Comprehensive Rites, the ritual institutions and ceremonial regulations held by the responsible offices ran to nearly several hundred separate works.

sentences.zh: 先是，天禧中，陳寬編次禮院所承新舊詔敕，不就。

translations.literal: Earlier, in the Tianxi era, Chen Kuan compiled the old and new edicts and orders received by the Court of Rites, but did not complete the work.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, during the Tianxi period, Chen Kuan undertook to compile the old and new edicts received by the Court of Rites, but never finished.

sentences.zh: 天聖初，王皞始類成書，盡乾興，為《禮閣新編》，大率禮文，無著述體，而本末完具，有司便之。

translations.literal: At the beginning of the Tiansheng era, Wang Hao first classified the materials into a completed book, extending through the Qianxing era, entitled New Compilation of the Ritual Archive; it was for the most part ritual texts, without the form of a composed treatise, yet beginning and end were complete, and the offices found it convenient.
translations.idiomatic: At the start of the Tiansheng reign, Wang Hao first arranged the materials into a finished compilation covering the period through Qianxing, entitled New Compilation of the Ritual Archive. It consisted chiefly of ritual texts rather than a formal treatise, yet was complete from start to finish and proved convenient for the responsible offices.

sentences.zh: 景祐四年，賈昌朝撰《太常新禮》及《祀儀》，止于慶曆三年。

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Jingyou, Jia Changchao compiled the New Rites of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices and the Sacrificial Protocols, ending in the third year of Qingli.
translations.idiomatic: In Jingyou 4 (1037), Jia Changchao compiled the New Rites of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices and the Sacrificial Protocols, bringing the record down to Qingli 3 (1043).

sentences.zh: 皇祐中，文彥博又撰《大享明堂記》二十卷。

translations.literal: In the Huangyou era, Wen Yanbo also compiled the Record of the Great Offering in the Bright Hall in twenty juan.
translations.idiomatic: During Huangyou, Wen Yanbo also compiled the Record of the Great Offering in the Bright Hall in twenty juan.

sentences.zh: 至嘉祐中，歐陽修纂集散失，命官設局，主《通禮》而記其變，及《新禮》以類相從，為一百卷，賜名《太常因革禮》，異于舊者蓋十三四焉。

translations.literal: By the Jiayou era, Ouyang Xiu gathered and edited what had been scattered and lost; officials were ordered to establish a bureau, taking the Comprehensive Rites as the main text while recording its changes, together with the New Rites arranged by category, making one hundred juan, granted the title Rites of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices on Continuity and Reform; what differed from the old was roughly three or four parts in ten.
translations.idiomatic: By the Jiayou period, Ouyang Xiu collected and edited scattered ritual materials. An official bureau was established to take the Comprehensive Rites as the foundation, record subsequent changes, and arrange the New Rites by category. The resulting work of one hundred juan was granted the title Rites of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices on Continuity and Reform; roughly thirty to forty percent differed from earlier practice.

sentences.zh: 熙寧十年，禮院取慶曆以後奉祀制度，別定《祀儀》，其一留中，其二付有司。

translations.literal: In the tenth year of Xining, the Ritual Court took sacrificial institutions after Qingli and separately fixed the Sacrificial Protocols; one copy was retained at court and two were delivered to the responsible offices.
translations.idiomatic: In Xining 10 (1077), the Ritual Court drew on sacrificial institutions after Qingli and separately fixed the Sacrificial Protocols; one copy was retained at court and two were delivered to the responsible offices.

sentences.zh: 知諫院黃履言：「郊祀禮樂，未合古制，請命有司考正群祀。」

translations.literal: Huang Lü, director of the Remonstrance Bureau, said: "The ritual and music of suburban sacrifice do not accord with ancient institutions; I request that the responsible offices examine and correct the various sacrifices."
translations.idiomatic: Huang Lü, director of the Remonstrance Bureau, said: "The ritual and music of suburban sacrifice do not accord with ancient institutions; I request that the responsible offices examine and correct the various sacrifices."

sentences.zh: 詔履與禮官講求以聞。

translations.literal: An edict ordered Lü and the ritual officials to investigate and report.
translations.idiomatic: An edict ordered Lü and the ritual officials to investigate and report.

sentences.zh: 元豐元年，始命太常寺置局，以樞密直學士陳襄等為詳定官，太常博士楊完等為檢討官。

translations.literal: In the first year of Yuanfeng, the Court of Imperial Sacrifices was first ordered to establish a bureau, with Hanlin academician of the Bureau of Military Affairs Chen Xiang and others as detailed determination officers and Court of Imperial Sacrifices doctors Yang Wan and others as collation officers.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Yuanfeng (1078), the Court of Imperial Sacrifices was first ordered to establish a bureau, with Hanlin academician of the Bureau of Military Affairs Chen Xiang and others as detailed determination officers and Court of Imperial Sacrifices doctors Yang Wan and others as collation officers.

sentences.zh: 襄等言：「國朝大率皆循唐故，至於壇壝神位、法駕輿輦、仗衛儀物，亦兼用歷代之制。

translations.literal: Chen Xiang and others said: 'Our dynasty for the most part follows Tang precedents; as for altar enclosures, spirit positions, imperial carriages and palanquins, and guard regalia and ceremonial objects, we also draw upon institutions of successive ages.
translations.idiomatic: Chen Xiang and others said: 'Our dynasty for the most part follows Tang precedents; as for altar enclosures, spirit positions, imperial carriages and palanquins, and guard regalia and ceremonial objects, we also draw upon institutions of successive ages.

sentences.zh: 其間情文訛舛，多戾于古。

translations.literal: Among these, sentiment and form are corrupted and erroneous, largely departing from antiquity.
translations.idiomatic: Among these, sentiment and form are corrupted and erroneous, largely departing from antiquity.

sentences.zh: 蓋有規摹苟略，因仍既久，而重于改作者；

translations.literal: Some have frameworks that are perfunctory and rough, have long been perpetuated, and are reluctant to be reworked;
translations.idiomatic: Some have frameworks that are perfunctory and rough, have long been perpetuated, and are reluctant to be reworked;

sentences.zh: 有出於一時之儀，而不足以為法者。

translations.literal: some arise from provisional rites of a single occasion and are insufficient to serve as precedent.
translations.idiomatic: some arise from provisional rites of a single occasion and are insufficient to serve as precedent.

sentences.zh: 請先條奏，候訓敕以為禮式。」

translations.literal: We request that items be submitted first in separate memorials, awaiting imperial instructions and edicts to establish them as ritual models.'
translations.idiomatic: We request that items be submitted first in separate memorials, awaiting imperial instructions and edicts to establish them as ritual models.'

sentences.zh: 未幾，又命龍圖直學士宋敏求同御史台、閣門、禮院詳定《朝會儀注》，總四十六卷：曰《閣門儀》，曰《朝會禮文》，曰《儀注》，曰《徽號寶冊儀》。

translations.literal: Before long, Song Minqiu, Hanlin academician of the Dragon Diagram Hall, was also ordered, together with the Censorate, the Gate Office, and the Ritual Court, to determine in detail the Court Assembly Ceremonial Protocols, altogether forty-six juan: entitled Gate Office Protocols, Court Assembly Ritual Texts, Ceremonial Protocols, and Protocols for Honorific Titles and Imperial Registers.
translations.idiomatic: Soon afterward Song Minqiu, academician of the Dragon Diagram Hall, was ordered together with the Censorate, the Gate Office, and the Ritual Court to compile the Court Assembly Ceremonial Protocols in forty-six juan: Gate Office Protocols, Court Assembly Ritual Texts, Ceremonial Protocols, and Protocols for Honorific Titles and Imperial Registers.

sentences.zh: 《祭祀》總百九十一卷：曰《祀儀》，曰《南郊式》，曰《大禮式》，曰《郊廟奉祀禮文》，曰《明堂袷享令式》，曰《天興殿儀》，曰《四孟朝獻儀》，曰《景靈宮供奉敕令格式》，曰《儀禮敕令格式》。

translations.literal: Sacrifices totaled one hundred ninety-one juan: entitled Sacrificial Protocols, Southern Suburb Forms, Great Rite Forms, Ritual Texts for Suburban and Temple Offerings, Bright Hall Joint-Offering Regulations and Forms, Hall of Heavenly Prosperity Protocols, Four-Season First-Month Presentation Protocols, Jingling Palace Offering Edicts and Formats, and Ritual Edicts and Formats.
translations.idiomatic: The section on Sacrifices ran to 191 juan: Sacrificial Protocols, Southern Suburb Forms, Great Rite Forms, Ritual Texts for Suburban and Temple Offerings, Bright Hall Joint-Offering Regulations and Forms, Hall of Heavenly Prosperity Protocols, Four-Season First-Month Presentation Protocols, Jingling Palace Offering Edicts and Formats, and Ritual Edicts and Formats.

sentences.zh: 《祈禳》總四十卷：曰《祀賽式》，曰《齋醮式》，曰《金籙儀》。

translations.literal: Prayer and Expiation totaled forty juan: entitled Forms for Sacrificial Thanksgiving, Forms for Fasting and Ritual Offerings, and Golden Register Protocols.
translations.idiomatic: Prayer and Expiation comprised forty juan: Forms for Sacrificial Thanksgiving, Forms for Fasting and Ritual Offerings, and Golden Register Protocols.

sentences.zh: 《蕃國》總七十一卷：曰《大遼令式》，曰《高麗入貢儀》，曰《女真排辦儀》，曰《諸蕃進貢令式》。

translations.literal: Foreign States totaled seventy-one juan: entitled Liao Regulations and Forms, Koryŏ Tribute-Entry Protocols, Jurchen Arrangement Protocols, and Regulations and Forms for Tribute from the Various Foreign States.
translations.idiomatic: Foreign States comprised seventy-one juan: Liao Regulations and Forms, Koryŏ Tribute-Entry Protocols, Jurchen Arrangement Protocols, and Regulations and Forms for Tribute from the Various Foreign States.

sentences.zh: 《喪葬》總百六十三卷：曰《葬式》，曰《宗室外臣葬敕令格式》，曰《孝贈式》。

translations.literal: Mourning and Burial totaled one hundred sixty-three juan: entitled Burial Forms, Edicts and Formats for Burial of Imperial Clansmen and Outer Officials, and Forms for Filial Bestowals.
translations.idiomatic: Mourning and Burial comprised 163 juan: Burial Forms, Edicts and Formats for Burial of Imperial Clansmen and Outer Officials, and Forms for Filial Bestowals.

sentences.zh: 其損益之制，視前多矣。

translations.literal: The regulations added and reduced were far more numerous than before.
translations.idiomatic: The additions and revisions far exceeded those of earlier compilations.

sentences.zh: 紹聖而後，累詔續編，起治平，訖政和，凡五十一年，為書三百卷，今皆不傳。

translations.literal: After Shaosheng, repeated edicts ordered continued compilation, from Zhiping through Zhenghe, altogether fifty-one years, making books of three hundred juan; none are extant today.
translations.idiomatic: After Shaosheng, repeated edicts ordered further compilation from Zhiping through Zhenghe—fifty-one years in all—producing three hundred juan of text, none of which survives today.

sentences.zh: 而大觀初，置議禮局於尚書省，命詳議、檢討官具禮制本末，議定請旨。

translations.literal: But at the beginning of Daguan, a Ritual Deliberation Bureau was established in the Department of State Affairs, with detailed deliberators and examining officers ordered to set forth the origins and ends of ritual institutions, deliberate, and submit decisions for imperial approval.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of the Daguan era, a Ritual Deliberation Bureau was established in the Department of State Affairs. Deliberators and examining officers were ordered to trace the origins of ritual institutions, reach decisions, and submit them for imperial approval.

sentences.zh: 三年書成，為《吉禮》二百三十一卷、《祭服制度》十六卷，頒焉。

translations.literal: In the third year the books were completed, comprising Auspicious Rites in two hundred thirty-one juan and Regulations for Sacrificial Garments in sixteen juan, which were promulgated.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year the compilation was finished: Auspicious Rites in 231 juan and Regulations for Sacrificial Garments in 16 juan, which were then promulgated.

sentences.zh: 議禮局請分秩五禮，詔依《開寶通禮》之序。

translations.literal: The Ritual Deliberation Bureau requested that the Five Rites be ranked in separate order; an edict followed the sequence of the Kaibao Comprehensive Rites.
translations.idiomatic: The Ritual Deliberation Bureau requested that the Five Rites be arranged in separate ranks; an edict ordered that the sequence follow the Kaibao Comprehensive Rites.

sentences.zh: 政和元年，續修成四百七十七卷，且命仿是修定儀注。

translations.literal: In the first year of Zhenghe, continued revision was completed in four hundred seventy-seven juan, and officials were also ordered to revise ceremonial protocols on the same model.
translations.idiomatic: In Zhenghe 1, the continued revision reached 477 juan, and officials were also ordered to revise ceremonial protocols along the same lines.

sentences.zh: 三年，《五禮新儀》成，凡二百二十卷，增置禮直官，許士庶就問新儀，而詔開封尹王革編類通行者，刊本給天下，使悉知禮意，其不奉行者論罪。

translations.literal: In the third year, the New Protocols of the Five Rites was completed, altogether two hundred twenty juan; ritual liaison officers were added, and commoners and officials were permitted to inquire about the new protocols. An edict ordered Kaifeng intendant Wang Ge to compile and classify what was generally applicable, print editions and distribute them throughout the realm so that all would know ritual meaning; those who did not comply were to be punished by law.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year the New Protocols of the Five Rites was completed in 220 juan. Additional ritual liaison officers were appointed, and scholars and commoners were allowed to consult them. The Kaifeng intendant Wang Ge was ordered to compile generally applicable provisions, print them, and distribute copies throughout the empire so that everyone would understand ritual norms; failure to comply was made punishable by law.

sentences.zh: 宣和初，有言其煩擾者，遂罷之。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Xuanhe, some said it was burdensome and vexatious, and it was thereupon abolished.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Xuanhe era, critics complained that the system was burdensome, and it was abolished.

sentences.zh: 初，議禮局之置也，詔求天下古器，更制尊、爵、鼎、彝之屬。

translations.literal: When the Ritual Deliberation Bureau was first established, an edict sought ancient vessels throughout the realm and ordered new manufacture of goblets, libation cups, tripods, and ritual vessels of that kind.
translations.idiomatic: When the Ritual Deliberation Bureau was first established, an edict called for ancient vessels from throughout the empire and ordered new versions of goblets, libation cups, tripods, and similar ritual implements.

sentences.zh: 其後，又置禮制局於編類御筆所。

translations.literal: Afterward, a Ritual Regulations Bureau was also established in the Imperial Brush Compilation Office.
translations.idiomatic: Later a Ritual Regulations Bureau was also set up within the Imperial Brush Compilation Office.

sentences.zh: 於是郊廟禋祀之器，多更其舊。

translations.literal: Thereupon the vessels for suburban and temple offerings were largely changed from the old forms.
translations.idiomatic: As a result, most of the vessels used in suburban and temple sacrifices were replaced.

sentences.zh: 既有詔討論冠服，遂廢靴用履，其他無所改議，而禮制局亦罷。

translations.literal: Once an edict had ordered discussion of caps and garments, boots were abolished and shoes were used instead; on other matters no changes were deliberated, and the Ritual Regulations Bureau was also dissolved.
translations.idiomatic: After an edict ordered discussion of caps and garments, boots were abolished in favor of shoes. No other changes were adopted, and the Ritual Regulations Bureau was dissolved.

sentences.zh: 大抵累朝典禮，講議最詳。

translations.literal: On the whole, the canonical rites of successive reigns were discussed and deliberated with the greatest detail.
translations.idiomatic: On the whole, the canonical rites of successive reigns were debated and refined with exceptional thoroughness.

sentences.zh: 祀禮修于元豐，而成於元祐，至崇寧復有所增損。

translations.literal: Sacrificial rites were revised in Yuanfeng and completed in Yuanyou; by Chongning there were further additions and reductions.
translations.idiomatic: Sacrificial rites were revised under Yuanfeng, completed under Yuanyou, and further modified under Chongning.

sentences.zh: 其存於有司者，惟《元豐郊廟禮文》及《政和五禮新儀》而已。

translations.literal: Of what remained with the responsible offices, only the Yuanfeng Suburban and Temple Ritual Texts and the Zhenghe New Protocols of the Five Rites survived.
translations.idiomatic: Of what survived in the hands of the responsible offices, only the Yuanfeng Suburban and Temple Ritual Texts and the Zhenghe New Protocols of the Five Rites remained.

sentences.zh: 乃若圜丘之罷合祭天地；

translations.literal: Such as abolishing at the Circular Mound the joint sacrifice to Heaven and Earth;
translations.idiomatic: Such as abolishing the joint sacrifice to Heaven and Earth at the Circular Mound;

sentences.zh: 明堂專以英宗配帝，悉罷從祀群神；

translations.literal: at the Bright Hall taking only Emperor Yingzong as correlate to the Thearch and abolishing all accompanying sacrifices to the host of spirits;
translations.idiomatic: at the Bright Hall pairing only Emperor Yingzong with the Thearch and abolishing all accompanying sacrifices to lesser spirits;

sentences.zh: 大蠟分四郊；

translations.literal: dividing the great la sacrifice among the four suburbs;
translations.idiomatic: dividing the great year-end la sacrifice among the four suburban altars;

sentences.zh: 壽星改祀老人；

translations.literal: changing the Longevity Star sacrifice to worship of the Old Man;
translations.idiomatic: changing the Longevity Star sacrifice to worship of the Old Man of the South Pole;

sentences.zh: 禧祖已祧而復，遂為始祖；

translations.literal: Ancestor Xi, though already removed in the distant shrine, was restored and thus made founding ancestor;
translations.idiomatic: Ancestor Xi, though already removed to the distant shrine, was restored and made founding ancestor;

sentences.zh: 即景靈宮建諸神禦殿，以四孟薦享；

translations.literal: at the Jingling Palace erecting halls for the spirits' imperial presence, with offerings in the four first months of the seasons;
translations.idiomatic: building spirit halls at the Jingling Palace for seasonal offerings in the four first months;

sentences.zh: 虛禘祭；

translations.literal: making the di offering void;
translations.idiomatic: abolishing the di offering;

sentences.zh: 去牙盤食；

translations.literal: removing tooth-tray food;
translations.idiomatic: eliminating tooth-tray offerings;

sentences.zh: 卻尊號；

translations.literal: declining honorific titles;
translations.idiomatic: refusing honorific titles;

sentences.zh: 罷入閣儀並常朝及正衙橫行。

translations.literal: abolishing the entering-the-pavilion ceremony together with regular court audiences and transverse processions in the main hall.
translations.idiomatic: abolishing the entering-the-pavilion ceremony, regular court audiences, and transverse processions in the main hall.

sentences.zh: 此熙甯、元豐變禮之最大者也。

translations.literal: These were the greatest changes in ritual under Xining and Yuanfeng.
translations.idiomatic: These were the greatest ritual reforms of the Xining and Yuanfeng periods.

sentences.zh: 元祐冊後，政和冠皇子，元符創景靈西宮，崇甯親祀方澤、作明堂、立九廟、鑄九鼎、祀熒惑，大觀受八寶、大祀皆前期十日而戒。

translations.literal: In Yuanyou the empress was invested; in Zhenghe the crown prince was capped; in Yuanfu the western Jingling Palace was founded; in Chongning the emperor personally sacrificed at the Square Pond, built the Bright Hall, established the nine temples, cast the nine tripods, and sacrificed to the Sparkling Deluder; in Daguan the Eight Treasures were received, and for all great sacrifices abstention was ordered ten days in advance.
translations.idiomatic: Under Yuanyou the empress was invested; under Zhenghe the crown prince received his capping; under Yuanfu the western Jingling Palace was founded; under Chongning the emperor personally sacrificed at the Square Pond, built the Bright Hall, established the nine temples, cast the nine tripods, and sacrificed to Mars; under Daguan the Eight Treasures were received, and for all great sacrifices a ten-day period of abstention was required in advance.

sentences.zh: 凡此蓋治平以前所未嘗行者。

translations.literal: All these were things never practiced before the Zhiping era.
translations.idiomatic: All of these were practices never undertaken before the Zhiping period.

sentences.zh: 欽宗即位，嘗詔春秋釋奠改從《元豐儀》，罷《新儀》不用而未暇也。

translations.literal: When Emperor Qinzong took the throne, he once ordered that the spring and autumn libation offerings follow the Yuanfeng Protocols and abandon the New Protocols, but there was no leisure to carry this out.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Qinzong ascended the throne, he ordered that the spring and autumn libation offerings follow the Yuanfeng Protocols rather than the New Protocols, but there was no time to implement the change.

sentences.zh: 靖康之厄，蕩析無餘。

translations.literal: In the calamity of Jingkang, everything was swept away without remainder.
translations.idiomatic: The Jingkang catastrophe swept everything away without a trace.

sentences.zh: 南渡中興，銳意修復，高宗嘗謂輔臣曰：「晉武平吳之後，上下不知有禮，旋致禍亂。

translations.literal: After crossing south and restoring the dynasty, there was keen intent to repair institutions. Emperor Gaozong once said to his chief ministers: 'After Jin Wudi pacified Wu, above and below no longer knew ritual, and disaster and rebellion soon followed.
translations.idiomatic: After the southward relocation and dynastic restoration, vigorous efforts were made to rebuild institutions. Emperor Gaozong once told his chief ministers: 'After Emperor Wu of Jin conquered Wu, court and people alike forgot ritual, and calamity followed swiftly.

sentences.zh: 周禮不秉，其何能國？」

translations.literal: If the Rites of Zhou are not upheld, how can there be a state?'
translations.idiomatic: Without upholding the Rites of Zhou, how can a state endure?'

sentences.zh: 孝宗繼志，典章文物，有可稱述。

translations.literal: Emperor Xiaozong carried on his intent; in statutes, regulations, and cultural institutions there was much worth recounting.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Xiaozong carried on this intent, and in statutes, regulations, and cultural institutions there was much worth recounting.

sentences.zh: 治平日久，經學大明，諸儒如王普、董{分廾}等多以禮名家。

translations.literal: As peace lasted long and classical learning flourished brightly, scholars such as Wang Pu, Dong Bi, and others became famous specialists in ritual.
translations.idiomatic: As peace endured and classical learning flourished, scholars such as Wang Pu and Dong Bi became renowned authorities on ritual.

sentences.zh: 當時嘗續編《太常因革禮》矣，淳熙復有編輯之旨。

translations.literal: At the time there was an attempt to continue compiling the Rites on Continuity and Reform; in Chunxi there was again an order to edit.
translations.idiomatic: At the time work was begun on a continuation of the Rites on Continuity and Reform, and under Chunxi there was again an order to compile.

sentences.zh: 其後朱熹講明詳備，嘗欲取《儀禮》、《周官》、《二戴記》為本，編次朝廷公卿大夫士民之禮，盡取漢、晉而下及唐諸儒之說，考訂辨正，以為當代之典，未及成書而沒。

translations.literal: Later Zhu Xi expounded with exhaustive completeness and once wished to take the Ceremonial Rites, the Offices of Zhou, and the two Dai ritual records as foundation, arranging in order the rites of court, nobles, grandees, officers, and commoners, taking fully the explanations of Han, Jin, and later scholars and Tang Confucians, examining, correcting, and distinguishing them to make the canon of the age, but died before the book was completed.
translations.idiomatic: Later Zhu Xi expounded ritual with exhaustive thoroughness. He once planned to take the Ceremonial Rites, the Offices of Zhou, and the two Dai ritual records as his foundation, arrange the rites of court, nobles, officials, and commoners in order, and incorporate the commentaries of scholars from Han and Jin onward through the Tang, revising and correcting them to establish a canon for the age—but he died before the work was finished.

sentences.zh: 理宗四十年間，屢有意乎禮文之事，雖曰崇尚理學，所謂「禮雲禮雲，玉帛雲乎哉」，蓋可三歎。

translations.literal: During Emperor Lizong's forty years there were repeated intentions regarding ritual texts; although Neo-Confucian learning was honored, as the saying goes, 'Ritual, ritual—is it only jade and silk?' One may sigh three times over this.
translations.idiomatic: During Emperor Lizong's forty-year reign there were repeated gestures toward ritual reform; although Neo-Confucian learning was honored, as the saying has it, 'Ritual, ritual—is it only jade and silk?' One can only sigh at the gap between aspiration and practice.

sentences.zh: 鹹淳以降，無足言者。

translations.literal: From Xianchun onward, there is nothing worth mentioning.
translations.idiomatic: From the Xianchun period onward, there is little worth recording.

sentences.zh: 今因前史之舊，芟其繁亂，匯為五禮，以備一代之制，使後之觀者有足征焉。

translations.literal: Now, following the precedent of earlier histories, we prune what is redundant and disorderly and gather it into the Five Rites to complete the institutions of the dynasty, so that later observers may have sufficient evidence.
translations.idiomatic: Following the precedent of earlier histories, we have pruned redundant and disorderly material and gathered it into the Five Rites to present the institutions of the dynasty complete, so that later readers may have adequate evidence.

sentences.zh: 五禮之序，以吉禮為首，主邦國神祇祭祀之事。

translations.literal: In the order of the Five Rites, Auspicious Rites come first, governing sacrifices to the spirits and deities of the state.
translations.idiomatic: Among the Five Rites, Auspicious Rites come first, governing sacrifices to the spirits and deities of the state.

sentences.zh: 凡祀典皆領于太常。

translations.literal: All sacrificial canons are overseen by the Court of Imperial Sacrifices.
translations.idiomatic: All sacrificial regulations are administered by the Court of Imperial Sacrifices.

sentences.zh: 歲之大祀三十：正月上辛祈谷，孟夏雩祀，季秋大享明堂，冬至圜丘祭昊天上帝，正月上辛又祀感生帝，四立及土王日祀五方帝，春分朝日，秋分夕月，東西太一，臘日大蠟祭百神，夏至祭皇地祇，孟冬祭神州地祇，四孟、季冬薦享太廟、後廟，春秋二仲及臘日祭太社、太稷，二仲九宮貴神。

translations.literal: The year's great sacrifices number thirty: on the first xin day of the first month, prayer for grain; in the first month of summer, rain prayer; in the last month of autumn, the great offering in the Bright Hall; at the winter solstice, sacrifice at the Circular Mound to August Heaven Thearch; on the first xin day of the first month, again sacrifice to the Life-Generating Thearch; at the four establishments and on earth-sovereign days, sacrifice to the Five Directional Thearchs; at the spring equinox, audience with the sun; at the autumn equinox, evening audience with the moon; eastern and western Grand Unity; on the la day, the great la sacrifice to the hundred spirits; at the summer solstice, sacrifice to August Earth; in the first month of winter, sacrifice to the Earth of the Divine Land; in the four first months and last month of winter, offerings at the Grand Temple and Rear Temple; in the two mid-seasons of spring and autumn and on the la day, sacrifice at the Grand Altars of Soil and Grain; in the two mid-seasons, the Nine Palaces Noble Spirit.
translations.idiomatic: There are thirty great annual sacrifices: on the first xin day of the first month, prayer for grain; in early summer, the rain prayer; in late autumn, the great offering in the Bright Hall; at the winter solstice, sacrifice at the Circular Mound to August Heaven; on the first xin day of the first month, sacrifice to the Life-Generating Thearch; at the four seasonal establishments and on earth-sovereign days, sacrifice to the Five Directional Thearchs; at the spring equinox, the morning rite to the sun; at the autumn equinox, the evening rite to the moon; eastern and western Grand Unity; on the la day, the great year-end sacrifice to the hundred spirits; at the summer solstice, sacrifice to August Earth; in early winter, sacrifice to the Earth of the Divine Land; in the four first months of the seasons and in late winter, offerings at the Grand Temple and Rear Temple; in the two mid-seasons of spring and autumn and on the la day, sacrifice at the Grand Altars of Soil and Grain; and in the two mid-seasons, the Nine Palaces Noble Spirit.

sentences.zh: 中祀九：仲春祭五龍，立春後醜日祀風師、亥日享先農，季春巳日享先蠶，立夏後申日祀雨師，春秋二仲上丁釋奠文宣王、上戊釋奠武成王。

translations.literal: Medium sacrifices number nine: in mid-spring, sacrifice to the Five Dragons; on the chou day after spring establishment, sacrifice to the Wind Master, and on the hai day, offering to the First Farmer; on the si day of the last month of spring, offering to the First Silkworm; on the shen day after summer establishment, sacrifice to the Rain Master; in the two mid-seasons of spring and autumn, on the upper ding day, libation offering to King Wenxuan, and on the upper wu day, libation offering to King Wucheng.
translations.idiomatic: There are nine medium sacrifices: in mid-spring, sacrifice to the Five Dragons; on the chou day after the start of spring, sacrifice to the Wind Master, and on the hai day, offering to the First Farmer; on the si day of late spring, offering to the First Silkworm; on the shen day after the start of summer, sacrifice to the Rain Master; and in the two mid-seasons of spring and autumn, on the upper ding day the libation offering to King Wenxuan and on the upper wu day the libation offering to King Wucheng.

sentences.zh: 小祀九：仲春祀馬祖，仲夏享先牧，仲秋祭馬社，仲冬祭馬步，季夏土王日祀中霤，立秋後辰日祀靈星，秋分享壽星，立冬後亥日祠司中、司命、司人、司祿，孟冬祭司寒。

translations.literal: Minor sacrifices number nine: in mid-spring, sacrifice to the Horse Ancestor; in mid-summer, offering to the First Herdsman; in mid-autumn, sacrifice at the Horse Earth Altar; in mid-winter, sacrifice at the Horse Step; in the last month of summer on the earth-sovereign day, sacrifice to the Central Drain; on the chen day after autumn establishment, sacrifice to the Spirit Star; at the autumn equinox, offering to the Longevity Star; on the hai day after winter establishment, sacrifice to the Directors of Center, Fate, Man, and Emolument; in the first month of winter, sacrifice to the Director of Cold.
translations.idiomatic: There are nine minor sacrifices: in mid-spring, the Horse Ancestor; in mid-summer, the First Herdsman; in mid-autumn, the Horse Earth Altar; in mid-winter, the Horse Step; in late summer on the earth-sovereign day, the Central Drain; on the chen day after the start of autumn, the Spirit Star; at the autumn equinox, the Longevity Star; on the hai day after the start of winter, the Directors of Center, Fate, Man, and Emolument; and in early winter, the Director of Cold.

sentences.zh: 其諸州奉祀，則五郊迎氣日祭嶽、鎮、海、瀆，春秋二仲享先代帝王及週六廟，並如中祀。

translations.literal: As for sacrifices performed in the various prefectures, on the five suburban days of receiving the qi they sacrifice to the peaks, prominences, seas, and streams; in the two mid-seasons of spring and autumn they offer to former dynastic emperors and the six temples of Zhou—all like medium sacrifices.
translations.idiomatic: Prefectural sacrifices include, on the five suburban days of receiving the seasonal qi, sacrifices to mountains, prominences, seas, and rivers; in the two mid-seasons of spring and autumn, offerings to emperors of former dynasties and the six Zhou temples—all treated as medium sacrifices.

sentences.zh: 州縣祭社稷，奠文宣王，祀風雨，並如小祀。

translations.literal: Prefectures and counties sacrifice at the altars of soil and grain, present offerings to King Wenxuan, and sacrifice to wind and rain—all like minor sacrifices.
translations.idiomatic: At the prefectural and county level, sacrifices to the altars of soil and grain, offerings to King Wenxuan, and sacrifices to wind and rain are all treated as minor sacrifices.

sentences.zh: 凡有大赦，則令諸州祭嶽、瀆、名山、大川在境內者，及歷代帝王、忠臣、烈士載祀典者，仍禁近祠廟鹹加祭。

translations.literal: Whenever there is a great amnesty, the various prefectures are ordered to sacrifice at mountains, streams, famous mountains, and great rivers within their borders, and at former dynastic emperors, loyal ministers, and martyrs recorded in the sacrificial canon; private temples nearby are still forbidden to add sacrifices.
translations.idiomatic: Whenever a great amnesty is proclaimed, prefectures are ordered to sacrifice at mountains, streams, famous mountains, and great rivers within their borders, and at emperors, loyal ministers, and martyrs listed in the sacrificial canon; nearby private temples are still forbidden to add unauthorized sacrifices.

sentences.zh: 有不克定時日者，太卜署預擇一季祠祭之日，謂之「畫日」。

translations.literal: When the date could not be fixed, the Grand Divination Office beforehand selected a season's days for temple sacrifice, called 'marked days.'
translations.idiomatic: When a date could not be fixed in advance, the Grand Divination Office selected seasonal days for sacrifice in advance; these were called 'marked days.'

sentences.zh: 凡壇壝、牲器、玉帛、饌具、齋戒之制，皆具《通禮》。

translations.literal: All regulations for altars, enclosures, sacrificial animals, vessels, jade and silk, food offerings, and abstention are fully set forth in the Comprehensive Rites.
translations.idiomatic: Regulations for altars, enclosures, sacrificial victims, vessels, jade and silk, food offerings, and abstention are all set forth in the Comprehensive Rites.

sentences.zh: 後復有高禖、大小酺神之屬，增大祀為四十二焉。

translations.literal: Later there were again the High Mei and greater and lesser Spirit of the Community, and the great sacrifices were increased to forty-two.
translations.idiomatic: Later the High Mei and greater and lesser Community Spirits were added, increasing the great sacrifices to forty-two.

sentences.zh: 其後，神宗詔改定大祀：太一，東以春，西以秋，中以夏冬；

translations.literal: Later, Emperor Shenzong ordered revision of the great sacrifices: Grand Unity—east in spring, west in autumn, center in summer and winter;
translations.idiomatic: Later Emperor Shenzong ordered a revision of the great sacrifices: Grand Unity in the east in spring, in the west in autumn, and in the center in summer and winter;

sentences.zh: 增大蠟為四，東西蠟主日配月；

translations.literal: the great la was increased to four; the eastern and western la took the sun as correlate and the moon as associate;
translations.idiomatic: the great la sacrifice was divided into four, with the eastern and western la pairing the sun with the moon;

sentences.zh: 太廟月祭朔。

translations.literal: the Grand Temple held monthly sacrifice on the new moon.
translations.idiomatic: the Grand Temple held monthly new-moon sacrifices.

sentences.zh: 而中祀：四望，南北蠟。

translations.literal: Among medium sacrifices: the Four Quarters, and the northern and southern la.
translations.idiomatic: Among medium sacrifices: the Four Quarters and the northern and southern la.

sentences.zh: 小祀：以四立祭司命、戶、灶、中霤、門、厲、行，以藏冰、出冰祭司寒，及月薦新太廟。

translations.literal: Minor sacrifices: at the four establishments, sacrifice to the Directors of Fate, Door, Stove, Central Drain, Gate, Pestilence, and Road; at storing ice and bringing out ice, sacrifice to the Director of Cold; and monthly presentation of new offerings at the Grand Temple.
translations.idiomatic: Minor sacrifices included, at the four seasonal establishments, the Directors of Fate, Door, Stove, Central Drain, Gate, Pestilence, and Road; at the storing and bringing out of ice, the Director of Cold; and monthly presentation of new offerings at the Grand Temple.

sentences.zh: 歲通舊祀凡九十二，惟五享後廟焉。

translations.literal: Sacrifices throughout the year according to the old totaled ninety-two, with only five offerings at the Rear Temple.
translations.idiomatic: Annual sacrifices under the old system totaled ninety-two, with only five offerings at the Rear Temple.

sentences.zh: 政和中，定《五禮新儀》，以熒惑、陽德觀、帝鼐、坊州朝獻聖祖、應天府祀大火為大祀；

translations.literal: In Zhenghe, when the New Protocols of the Five Rites was fixed, Mars, the Hall of Yang Virtue, Emperor Nai, Fangzhou's presentation to the Sage Ancestor, and Yingtianfu's sacrifice to the Great Fire were made great sacrifices;
translations.idiomatic: Under Zhenghe, when the New Protocols of the Five Rites was established, Mars, the Hall of Yang Virtue, Emperor Nai, Fangzhou's presentation to the Sage Ancestor, and Yingtianfu's sacrifice to the Great Fire were classified as great sacrifices;

sentences.zh: 雷神、歷代帝王、寶鼎、牡鼎、蒼鼎、岡鼎、彤鼎、阜鼎、皛鼎、魁鼎、會應廟、慶厲軍祭後土為中祀；

translations.literal: the Thunder Spirit, emperors of successive dynasties, the Treasure Tripod, Ox Tripod, Azure Tripod, Hill Tripod, Red Tripod, Mound Tripod, White Tripod, and Chief Tripod, the Hall of Responsive Meeting, and Qingli Army's sacrifice to Queen Earth were made medium sacrifices;
translations.idiomatic: the Thunder Spirit, emperors of successive dynasties, the nine tripods (Treasure, Ox, Azure, Hill, Red, Mound, White, and Chief), the Hall of Responsive Meeting, and Qingli Army's sacrifice to Queen Earth were classified as medium sacrifices;

sentences.zh: 山林川澤之屬，州縣祭社稷、祀風伯雨師雷神為小祀。

translations.literal: mountains, forests, rivers, and marshes and the like, and prefectural and county sacrifices to the altars of soil and grain and to the Lords of Wind, Rain, and Thunder were minor sacrifices.
translations.idiomatic: mountains, forests, rivers, and marshes, together with prefectural and county sacrifices to the altars of soil and grain and to the Lords of Wind, Rain, and Thunder, were classified as minor sacrifices.

sentences.zh: 餘悉如故。

translations.literal: The rest remained entirely as before.
translations.idiomatic: Everything else remained unchanged.

sentences.zh: 建炎四年十一月，權工部尚書韓肖胄言：「祖宗以來，每歲大、中、小祀百有餘所，罔敢廢闕。

translations.literal: In the eleventh month of the fourth year of Jianyan, Acting Minister of Works Han Xiaozhou said: 'Since the founding ancestors, each year there have been more than a hundred great, medium, and minor sacrifices, none of which we dared neglect.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh month of Jianyan 4 (1130), Acting Minister of Works Han Xiaozhou said: 'Since the founding of the dynasty, more than a hundred great, medium, and minor sacrifices have been held each year, and none was ever allowed to lapse.

sentences.zh: 自車駕巡幸，惟存宗廟之祭，至天地諸神之祀，則廢而不舉。

translations.literal: Since the imperial carriage went on tour, only the ancestral temple sacrifices have been kept; as for sacrifices to Heaven, Earth, and the various spirits, they have been abandoned and not performed.
translations.idiomatic: Since the imperial court went on the move, only ancestral temple sacrifices have been maintained, while sacrifices to Heaven, Earth, and the various spirits have been abandoned.

sentences.zh: 今國步尚艱，天未悔禍，正宜齋明恭肅，通於神明，而忽大事、棄重禮，恐非所以消弭天災，導迎景貺。

translations.literal: Now the state's course is still difficult and Heaven has not yet turned from calamity; it is precisely the time to be pure, bright, reverent, and solemn and communicate with the spirits—yet to neglect great affairs and abandon weighty rites is surely not the way to dispel heavenly disasters and guide in bright blessings.
translations.idiomatic: The realm is still in distress and Heaven has not yet withdrawn its calamity. This is precisely the time for purity, reverence, and solemn communion with the spirits—yet to neglect great sacrifices and abandon weighty rites is surely not the way to dispel heavenly disasters and draw down blessings.

sentences.zh: 雖小祀未可遍舉，如天地、五帝、日月星辰、社稷，欲詔有司以時舉行。

translations.literal: Although minor sacrifices cannot all be performed, such as Heaven and Earth, the Five Thearchs, sun, moon, stars, and constellations, and the altars of soil and grain—I wish that the responsible offices be ordered to perform them on schedule.
translations.idiomatic: Although minor sacrifices cannot all be restored at once, I ask that responsible offices be ordered to perform sacrifices to Heaven and Earth, the Five Thearchs, the sun, moon, stars, and constellations, and the altars of soil and grain on schedule.

sentences.zh: 所有器服並牲牢禮料，恐國用未充，難如舊制，乞下太常寺相度裁定，省繁就簡，庶幾神不乏祀，仰副陛下昭事懷柔、為民求福之意。」

translations.literal: As for all vessels, garments, sacrificial animals, and ritual materials, I fear state revenue is insufficient to match the old system. I beg that the Court of Imperial Sacrifices be ordered to assess and determine, reducing complexity and adopting simplicity, so that the spirits may not lack sacrifice and thereby fulfill Your Majesty's intent of bright service, gentle cherishing, and seeking blessings for the people.'
translations.idiomatic: As for vessels, garments, sacrificial victims, and ritual materials, state revenue may be insufficient to match the old standards. I ask that the Court of Imperial Sacrifices assess what is needed, simplify where possible, and ensure that the spirits are not left without offerings—thereby fulfilling Your Majesty's intent to serve Heaven with clarity, cherish the people, and seek their welfare.'

sentences.zh: 尋命禮部太常裁定：每歲以立春上辛祀谷，孟夏雩祀，季秋及冬至日四祀天，夏至日一祀地，立春上辛日祀感生帝，立冬後祀神州地祇，春秋二社及臘前一日祭太社、太稷。

translations.literal: Shortly afterward the Ministry of Rites and Court of Imperial Sacrifices were ordered to determine: each year on the first xin day of spring establishment, sacrifice to the grain spirit; in the first month of summer, rain prayer; in the last month of autumn and on the winter solstice, four sacrifices to Heaven; on the summer solstice, one sacrifice to Earth; on the first xin day of spring establishment, sacrifice to the Life-Generating Thearch; after winter establishment, sacrifice to the Earth of the Divine Land; in spring and autumn the two she days and on the day before la, sacrifice at the Grand Altars of Soil and Grain.
translations.idiomatic: The Ministry of Rites and Court of Imperial Sacrifices were soon ordered to determine the schedule: each year on the first xin day of spring, sacrifice to the grain spirit; in early summer, the rain prayer; in late autumn and on the winter solstice, four sacrifices to Heaven; on the summer solstice, one sacrifice to Earth; on the first xin day of spring, sacrifice to the Life-Generating Thearch; after the start of winter, sacrifice to the Earth of the Divine Land; and in spring and autumn on the two she days and on the day before la, sacrifice at the Grand Altars of Soil and Grain.

sentences.zh: 免牲、玉，權用酒酺，仍依方色奠幣。

translations.literal: Victims and jade were waived; wine and fermented grain were used provisionally, while silks were still offered according to directional color.
translations.idiomatic: Sacrificial animals and jade were waived; wine and fermented grain were used instead, while silks were still offered according to directional color.

sentences.zh: 以輔臣為初獻，禮官為亞、終獻。

translations.literal: Chief ministers served as first offerers and ritual officials as second and final offerers.
translations.idiomatic: Chief ministers served as first offerers and ritual officials as second and final offerers.

sentences.zh: 紹興三年，復大火祀，配以閼伯，以辰、戌出納之月祀之。

translations.literal: In the third year of Shaoxing, sacrifice to the Great Fire was restored, with Que Bo as correlate, sacrificed in the months of chen and xu when it enters and exits.
translations.idiomatic: In Shaoxing 3 (1133), sacrifice to the Great Fire was restored, with Que Bo as correlate, performed in the chen and xu months when the star enters and exits its mansion.

sentences.zh: 二十七年，禮部太常寺言：「每歲大祀三十六，除天地、宗廟、社稷、感生帝、九宮貴神、高禖、文宣王等已行外，其餘並乞寓祠齋宮。」

translations.literal: In the twenty-seventh year, the Ministry of Rites and Court of Imperial Sacrifices said: 'Each year there are thirty-six great sacrifices; apart from Heaven and Earth, ancestral temples, altars of soil and grain, the Life-Generating Thearch, the Nine Palaces Noble Spirit, the High Mei, King Wenxuan, and others already performed, for the rest we request surrogate sacrifice at the Abstinence Palace.'
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-seventh year (1157), the Ministry of Rites and Court of Imperial Sacrifices reported: 'There are thirty-six great sacrifices each year. Apart from those already performed—Heaven and Earth, ancestral temples, altars of soil and grain, the Life-Generating Thearch, the Nine Palaces Noble Spirit, the High Mei, and King Wenxuan—we request that the remainder be performed by surrogate sacrifice at the Abstinence Palace.'

sentences.zh: 自紹興以來，大祀所行二十有三而已，至是乃悉復之。

translations.literal: Since Shaoxing, only twenty-three great sacrifices had been performed; now all were fully restored.
translations.idiomatic: Since the Shaoxing era only twenty-three great sacrifices had been performed; now all were fully restored.

sentences.zh: 舊制，郊廟祝文稱嗣皇帝，諸祭稱皇帝。

translations.literal: Under the old system, suburban and temple prayer texts used 'Heir Emperor,' and other sacrifices used 'Emperor.'
translations.idiomatic: Under the old system, suburban and temple prayer texts addressed the 'Heir Emperor,' while other sacrifices used simply 'Emperor.'

sentences.zh: 著作局准《開元禮》全稱帝號。

translations.literal: The Composition Office followed the Kaiyuan Rites in using the full imperial title.
translations.idiomatic: The Composition Office followed the Kaiyuan Rites in using the emperor's full title.

sentences.zh: 真宗以兼秘書監李至請，改從舊制。

translations.literal: Emperor Zhenzong, on the request of Li Zhi, concurrent director of the Secretariat, changed back to the old system.
translations.idiomatic: At the request of Li Zhi, concurrent director of the Secretariat, Emperor Zhenzong restored the old usage.

sentences.zh: 又諸祭祝辭皆臨事撰進，多違典禮，乃命至增撰舊辭八十四首，為《正辭錄》三卷。

translations.literal: Moreover, prayer texts for all sacrifices were composed and submitted on the spot, often violating canonical ritual; Li Zhi was therefore ordered to expand and compile eighty-four old prayers into the Correct Prayer Record in three juan.
translations.idiomatic: Moreover, prayer texts for sacrifices were often composed on the spot and violated canonical ritual. Li Zhi was ordered to compile eighty-four standard prayers into the Correct Prayer Record in three juan.

sentences.zh: 既復命知制誥李宗諤、楊億、直史館陳彭年詳定之，以為永式。

translations.literal: They were then ordered to be determined in detail by drafting edict officials Li Zong'e and Yang Yi and Hanlin compiler Chen Pengnian, and established as a permanent standard.
translations.idiomatic: Drafting edict officials Li Zong'e and Yang Yi and Hanlin compiler Chen Pengnian were then ordered to revise them in detail and establish them as the permanent standard.

sentences.zh: 祝版當進署者，並命秘閣吏書，上親署訖，禦寶封給之。

translations.literal: Prayer boards requiring presentation for signature were all ordered written by Secretariat clerks; after the emperor personally signed them, the imperial seal was applied and they were sealed and issued.
translations.idiomatic: Prayer boards requiring the emperor's signature were written by Secretariat clerks; after the emperor signed them personally, the imperial seal was applied and they were issued.

sentences.zh: 凡先代帝王，祝文止稱廟號。

translations.literal: For all emperors of former dynasties, prayer texts used only temple names.
translations.idiomatic: For emperors of former dynasties, prayer texts used only their temple names.

sentences.zh: 凡親行大祀，則皇子弟為亞獻、終獻。

translations.literal: Whenever the emperor personally performed a great sacrifice, imperial princes served as second and final offerers.
translations.idiomatic: When the emperor personally performed a great sacrifice, imperial princes served as second and final offerers.

sentences.zh: 五代以來，宰相為大禮使，太常卿為禮儀使，御史中丞為儀仗使，兵部尚書為鹵簿使，京府尹為橋道頓遞使。

translations.literal: Since the Five Dynasties, the chief minister was Grand Rite Commissioner, the Court of Imperial Sacrifices director was Ritual Protocol Commissioner, the censor-in-chief was Ceremonial Arms Commissioner, the minister of war was Insignia Commissioner, and the capital prefect was Bridge-Road and Relay Commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: Since the Five Dynasties, the chief minister served as Grand Rite Commissioner, the director of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices as Ritual Protocol Commissioner, the censor-in-chief as Ceremonial Arms Commissioner, the minister of war as Insignia Commissioner, and the capital prefect as Bridge-Road and Relay Commissioner.

sentences.zh: 至是，大禮使或用親王，禮儀使專命翰林學士，儀仗、鹵簿使亦或以他官。

translations.literal: By this time, the Grand Rite Commissioner might be an imperial prince; the Ritual Protocol Commissioner was exclusively a Hanlin academician; and the Ceremonial Arms and Insignia commissioners might also be other officials.
translations.idiomatic: By this time the Grand Rite Commissioner might be an imperial prince, the Ritual Protocol Commissioner was always a Hanlin academician, and the Ceremonial Arms and Insignia commissioners might be other officials.

sentences.zh: 太平興國九年，始鑄五使印。

translations.literal: In the ninth year of Taiping Xingguo, the seals of the five commissioners were first cast.
translations.idiomatic: In Taiping Xingguo 9 (984), the seals of the five commissioners were first cast.

sentences.zh: 太宗將封泰山，以儀仗使兼判橋道頓遞事。

translations.literal: When Emperor Taizong was about to perform the feng on Mount Tai, the Ceremonial Arms Commissioner was also made concurrent administrator of bridge-road and relay affairs.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Taizong prepared to perform the feng rites on Mount Tai, the Ceremonial Arms Commissioner was also assigned to oversee bridge, road, and relay affairs.

sentences.zh: 大中祥符後，凡有大禮，以中書、樞密分為五使，仍特鑄印。

translations.literal: After Dazhong Xiangfu, whenever there was a great rite, the Secretariat and Bureau of Military Affairs divided the five commissions, and special seals were still cast.
translations.idiomatic: After Dazhong Xiangfu (1008–1016), whenever a great rite was held, the Secretariat and Bureau of Military Affairs divided responsibility for the five commissions, and special seals were cast for the occasion.

sentences.zh: 景祐二年，詔有司：「皇地祇、神州，舊常參官攝事，非所以尊神，自今命兩省。

translations.literal: In the second year of Jingyou, an edict ordered the responsible offices: 'August Earth and the Earth of the Divine Land were formerly administered by regular attendees as surrogates—this is not how to honor the spirits. From now on the Two Departments are to be ordered.
translations.idiomatic: In Jingyou 2 (1035), an edict ordered: 'Sacrifices to August Earth and the Earth of the Divine Land were formerly performed by regular court attendees as surrogates—this does not properly honor the spirits. Henceforth the Two Departments shall be responsible.

sentences.zh: 歲九大祠，宰臣攝事者，參知政事、尚書丞郎、學士奉祠。」

translations.literal: For the nine annual great sacrifices at which chief ministers served as surrogates, vice grand councilors, secretaries and directors of the Ministries, and academicians performed the sacrifices.'
translations.idiomatic: For the nine annual great sacrifices at which chief ministers served as surrogates, vice grand councilors, ministry directors, and academicians performed the rites.'

sentences.zh: 於是參知政事盛度，享太廟已受誓戒，除知樞密院，乃不奉祠。

translations.literal: Thereupon Vice Grand Councilor Sheng Du, having already received abstention for offering at the Grand Temple, was appointed to the Bureau of Military Affairs and therefore did not perform the sacrifice.
translations.idiomatic: Vice Grand Councilor Sheng Du had already undertaken abstention for the Grand Temple offering when he was appointed to the Bureau of Military Affairs and therefore could not perform the sacrifice.

sentences.zh: 又故事，三歲一親郊，不郊輒代以他禮，慶賞與郊同，而五使皆以輔臣，不以官之高下。

translations.literal: By precedent also, every three years there was a personal suburban sacrifice; if no suburban sacrifice was held, another rite was substituted, rewards being the same as for the suburban sacrifice, and all five commissioners were chief ministers, without regard to rank.
translations.idiomatic: By precedent, the emperor performed the suburban sacrifice personally every three years; when he did not, another rite was substituted with the same rewards as for the suburban sacrifice. All five commissioners were chief ministers, regardless of rank.

sentences.zh: 天聖中，乃以朝林學士領儀仗，御史中丞領鹵簿，始用官次。

translations.literal: In Tiansheng, a Hanlin academician was made to head ceremonial arms and the censor-in-chief to head insignia, and official rank was first used.
translations.idiomatic: During Tiansheng, a Hanlin academician was appointed to head ceremonial arms and the censor-in-chief to head insignia—official rank was used for the first time.

sentences.zh: 又每歲大祀，皆遣台省近臣攝太尉，其後或委他官，太中祥符始復舊制。

translations.literal: Moreover, for each year's great sacrifices, a nearby official of the Censorate and Secretariat was sent as surrogate Grand Commandant; later this was sometimes delegated to other officials, and only in Dazhong Xiangfu was the old system restored.
translations.idiomatic: Each year a nearby Censorate or Secretariat official served as surrogate Grand Commandant for great sacrifices; later other officials were sometimes appointed, and the old practice was restored only under Dazhong Xiangfu.

sentences.zh: 又國朝沿唐制，以太尉掌誓戒。

translations.literal: The dynasty also followed Tang practice in having the Grand Commandant preside over abstention.
translations.idiomatic: The dynasty also followed Tang practice in entrusting abstention to the Grand Commandant.

sentences.zh: 今議太尉三公，非其所任，請以吏部尚書掌誓戒。

translations.literal: It was now argued that the Three Excellencies of Grand Commandant were not appropriate to this duty and that the minister of personnel should preside over abstention.
translations.idiomatic: It was argued that the Grand Commandant among the Three Excellencies was not suited to this duty and that the minister of personnel should preside over abstention instead.

sentences.zh: 詔用左僕射，闕則用右僕射、刑部尚書一員蒞之。

translations.literal: An edict ordered use of the left vice director; if absent, the right vice director or one minister of justice would attend.
translations.idiomatic: An edict ordered that the left vice director preside; if he was unavailable, the right vice director or the minister of justice would attend.

sentences.zh: 熙寧四年，參知政事王珪言：「南郊，乘輿所過，必勘箭然後出入，此師行之法，不可施於郊祀。」

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Xining, Vice Grand Councilor Wang Gui said: 'At the southern suburb, wherever the imperial carriage passed, tally arrows had to be checked before entry and exit—this is the method of military marches and cannot be applied to suburban sacrifice.'
translations.idiomatic: In Xining 4 (1071), Vice Grand Councilor Wang Gui said: 'At the southern suburb, wherever the imperial carriage passes, tally arrows must be checked before gates may open—this is a military procedure and should not be applied to suburban sacrifice.'

sentences.zh: 禮院亦言。

translations.literal: The Ritual Court also spoke likewise.
translations.idiomatic: The Ritual Court made the same recommendation.

sentences.zh: 於是，凡車駕出入門皆罷之。

translations.literal: Thereupon, for all gates through which the imperial carriage passed, this was abolished.
translations.idiomatic: Thereupon the practice was abolished at all gates used by the imperial carriage.

sentences.zh: 六年，以詳定所請，又罷太廟及宣德、朱雀、南薰諸門勘契。

translations.literal: In the sixth year, on request of the detailed determination office, tally inspection at the Grand Temple and at the Xuande, Zhuque, and Nanxun gates was also abolished.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth year, at the request of the detailed determination office, tally inspection was also abolished at the Grand Temple and at the Xuande, Zhuque, and Nanxun gates.

sentences.zh: 又皇帝自大次至版位，內臣二人執翟羽前導，號曰「拂翟」，失禮尤甚，請除之。

translations.literal: Moreover, when the emperor went from the great tent to the spirit tablet position, two inner attendants held pheasant feathers to lead ahead, called 'brushing the pheasant'—a violation of ritual especially grave; it was requested that this be removed.
translations.idiomatic: Moreover, when the emperor proceeded from the great tent to the spirit tablet, two inner attendants led the way holding pheasant feathers in a practice called 'brushing the pheasant'—a grave breach of ritual that was ordered abolished.

sentences.zh: 凡郊壇，值雨雪，即齋宮門望祭殿望拜，祭日不設登歌，祀官以公服行事，中祀以上皆給明衣。

translations.literal: Whenever at suburban altars there was rain or snow, from the Abstinence Palace gate they gazed toward the sacrifice hall and performed distant obeisance; on the sacrifice day elevated song was not set up; sacrifice officials acted in court dress; for medium sacrifices and above, bright garments were all provided.
translations.idiomatic: When rain or snow fell at suburban altars, officials performed distant obeisance from the Abstinence Palace gate toward the sacrifice hall; on the sacrifice day elevated song was omitted; sacrifice officials wore court dress; and for medium sacrifices and above, bright garments were provided.

sentences.zh: 開寶元年十一月郊，以燎壇稍遠，不聞告燎之聲，始用爟火，令光明遠照，通於祀所。

translations.literal: At the suburban sacrifice of the eleventh month of the first year of Kaibao, because the pyre altar was somewhat distant and the announcement of the pyre could not be heard, torch fire was first used, making light shine far and reach the place of sacrifice.
translations.idiomatic: At the suburban sacrifice of Kaibao 1 (968), because the pyre altar was distant and the pyre announcement could not be heard, torch fires were introduced so that their light would reach the sacrifice site.

sentences.zh: 又太廟初獻，依開寶例，以玉斝、玉瓚，亞獻以金斝，終獻以瓢斝。

translations.literal: At the Grand Temple first offering, following the Kaibao precedent, jade jia and jade guan were used; the second offering used gold jia, and the final offering gourd jia.
translations.idiomatic: At the Grand Temple, the first offering followed Kaibao precedent with jade jia and jade guan vessels; the second offering used gold jia, and the final offering gourd jia.

sentences.zh: 外壇器亦如之。

translations.literal: Vessels at the outer altar were the same.
translations.idiomatic: The outer altar used the same vessels.

sentences.zh: 慶曆中，太常請皇帝獻天地、配帝以匏爵，亞獻以木爵。

translations.literal: In Qingli, the Court of Imperial Sacrifices requested that the emperor offer to Heaven and Earth and the correlate thearch with gourd goblets, and the second offering use wooden goblets.
translations.idiomatic: During Qingli, the Court of Imperial Sacrifices requested that the emperor use gourd goblets when offering to Heaven and Earth and the correlate thearch, and wooden goblets for the second offering.

sentences.zh: 親祠太廟，酌以玉斝，亞獻以金斝。

translations.literal: When the emperor personally sacrificed at the Grand Temple, he poured with jade jia and the second offering used gold jia.
translations.idiomatic: When the emperor personally sacrificed at the Grand Temple, he poured with jade jia and the second offering used gold jia.

sentences.zh: 郊廟飲福，皇帝皆以玉斝。

translations.literal: For drinking blessing at suburban altars and temples, the emperor always used jade jia.
translations.idiomatic: For the blessing drink at suburban altars and temples, the emperor always used jade jia.

sentences.zh: 詔飲福，唯用金斝。

translations.literal: An edict ordered that for drinking blessing only gold jia be used.
translations.idiomatic: An edict ordered that only gold jia be used for the blessing drink.

sentences.zh: 亞、終獻，酌以銀斝。

translations.literal: Second and final offerings poured with silver jia.
translations.idiomatic: The second and final offerings used silver jia.

sentences.zh: 至飲福，尚食奉禦酌上尊酒，投溫器以進。

translations.literal: For drinking blessing, the Imperial Kitchen served the emperor, pouring supreme wine and warming it in a vessel before presenting it.
translations.idiomatic: For the blessing drink, the Imperial Kitchen served the emperor supreme wine, warming it before presentation.

sentences.zh: 凡常祀，天地宗廟，皆內降禦封香，仍制漆匱，付光祿、司農寺。

translations.literal: For all regular sacrifices to Heaven, Earth, and ancestral temples, imperially sealed incense was sent from within, and lacquer cases were made and entrusted to the Courts of Imperial Entertainments and Agriculture.
translations.idiomatic: For all regular sacrifices to Heaven, Earth, and the ancestral temples, imperially sealed incense was issued from within the palace, placed in lacquer cases, and entrusted to the Courts of Imperial Entertainments and Agriculture.

sentences.zh: 每祠祭，命判寺官緘署禮料送祀所。

translations.literal: For each temple sacrifice, the acting director of the court was ordered to seal and sign the ritual materials and send them to the sacrifice site.
translations.idiomatic: For each sacrifice, the acting director of the court was ordered to seal and sign the ritual materials and deliver them to the sacrifice site.

sentences.zh: 凡祈告，亦內出香。

translations.literal: For all prayer announcements, incense also came from within.
translations.idiomatic: Incense for prayer announcements was also issued from within the palace.

sentences.zh: 遂為定制。

translations.literal: This then became fixed regulation.
translations.idiomatic: This became established practice.

sentences.zh: 嘉祐中，裴煜請：「大祠悉降禦封香，中、小祠供太府香。

translations.literal: In Jiayou, Pei Yu requested: 'For all great sacrifices let imperially sealed incense be sent down; for medium and minor sacrifices let the Court of the Imperial Treasury supply incense.
translations.idiomatic: In Jiayou, Pei Yu requested: 'Let all great sacrifices receive imperially sealed incense; let medium and minor sacrifices be supplied with incense from the Imperial Treasury.

sentences.zh: 中祠減大祠之半，小祠減中祠之半。

translations.literal: Medium sacrifices were reduced to half of great sacrifices, minor sacrifices to half of medium sacrifices.
translations.idiomatic: Medium sacrifices received half the incense of great sacrifices, and minor sacrifices half that of medium sacrifices.

sentences.zh: 東、西太一宮系大祠，歲太府供香，非時祈請，降禦封香准大祠例。

translations.literal: The eastern and western Grand Unity Palaces ranked as great sacrifices; each year the Imperial Treasury supplied incense; for unscheduled prayers, imperially sealed incense was sent down according to the great sacrifice precedent.
translations.idiomatic: The eastern and western Grand Unity Palaces ranked as great sacrifices and received annual incense from the Imperial Treasury; for unscheduled prayers, imperially sealed incense was issued according to the great-sacrifice standard.

sentences.zh: 及皇地祇、五方帝、百神、文宣、武成從配神位，牲牢寡薄。」

translations.literal: As for August Earth, the Five Directional Thearchs, the hundred spirits, and the accompanying spirit positions of Wenxuan and Wucheng, sacrificial victims were scant.'
translations.idiomatic: Sacrificial victims were inadequate for August Earth, the Five Directional Thearchs, the hundred spirits, and the accompanying positions of Kings Wenxuan and Wucheng.'

sentences.zh: 呂公著亦論廟牲未備，悉加其數。

translations.literal: Lü Gongzhu also argued that temple victims were not sufficient and all numbers were increased.
translations.idiomatic: Lü Gongzhu also argued that temple victims were insufficient, and their numbers were all increased.

sentences.zh: 元符元年，左司員外郎曾旼言：「周人以氣臭事神，近世易之以香。

translations.literal: In the first year of Yuanfu, Left Office outer courtier Zeng Min said: 'The Zhou served the spirits with qi and odor; recent ages have replaced this with incense.
translations.idiomatic: In Yuanfu 1 (1098), Left Office outer courtier Zeng Min said: 'The Zhou served the spirits with the odors of burning offerings; recent times have replaced this with incense.

sentences.zh: 按何佟之議，以為南郊、明堂用沉香，本天之質，陽所宜也；

translations.literal: According to He Tongzhi's discussion, it was held that the southern suburb and Bright Hall use agarwood, which is the substance of Heaven and what yang should use;
translations.idiomatic: Following He Tongzhi's argument, agarwood was used at the southern suburb and Bright Hall because it is the substance of Heaven and appropriate to yang;

sentences.zh: 北效用上和香，以地於人親，宜加雜馥。

translations.literal: the northern suburb uses superior blended incense, since Earth is close to man and mixed fragrances are fitting.
translations.idiomatic: the northern suburb uses superior blended incense, since Earth is close to humanity and mixed fragrances are appropriate.

sentences.zh: 今令文北極天皇而下皆用濕香，至於眾星之位，香不復設，恐於義未盡。」

translations.literal: Now the regulations from the Pole Star Thearch downward all use moist incense, but for the positions of the host of stars incense is no longer set out—this may not fully accord with principle.'
translations.idiomatic: Current regulations require moist incense from the Pole Star Thearch downward, yet no incense is set out for the host of stars—this may not fully accord with ritual principle.'

sentences.zh: 於是每陛各設香。

translations.literal: Thereupon incense was set out at each terrace.
translations.idiomatic: Incense was then set out at each terrace level.

sentences.zh: 又言：「先儒以為實柴所祀者無玉，郐鍮燎所祀者無幣。

translations.literal: He also said: 'Former scholars held that those sacrificed to by solid firewood had no jade, and those sacrificed to by Zheng and You burning had no silks.
translations.idiomatic: He also said: 'Earlier scholars held that sacrifices offered on solid firewood altars required no jade, and those offered by Zheng and You burning required no silks.

sentences.zh: 今太常令式，眾星皆不用幣，蓋出於此。

translations.literal: Now in the Court of Imperial Sacrifices regulations, the host of stars all use no silks—this probably derives from that.
translations.idiomatic: The current Court of Imperial Sacrifices regulations provide no silks for the host of stars—probably deriving from this view.

sentences.zh: 然考《典瑞》、《玉人》之官，皆曰'圭璧以祀日月星辰'。

translations.literal: Yet examining the offices of Regalia and Jade Workers, both say 'gui and bi to sacrifice to sun, moon, stars, and constellations.'
translations.idiomatic: Yet the offices of Regalia and Jade Workers both state that 'gui and bi are used to sacrifice to the sun, moon, stars, and constellations.'

sentences.zh: 則實柴所祀非無玉矣。

translations.literal: Thus those sacrificed to by solid firewood were not without jade.
translations.idiomatic: Sacrifices on solid firewood altars were not without jade after all.

sentences.zh: 郐鍮燎無幣，恐或未然。」

translations.literal: That Zheng and You burning had no silks may perhaps not be so.'
translations.idiomatic: The claim that Zheng and You burning required no silks may also be incorrect.'

sentences.zh: 至是遂命眾星隨其方色用幣。

translations.literal: At this point it was ordered that the host of stars use silks according to their directional colors.
translations.idiomatic: The host of stars were then ordered to use silks according to their directional colors.

sentences.zh: 慶曆三年，禮官余靖言：「祈穀、祀感生帝同日，其禮當異，不可皆用四圭有邸，色尚赤。」

translations.literal: In the third year of Qingli, ritual official Yu Jing said: 'Prayer for grain and sacrifice to the Life-Generating Thearch fall on the same day; their rites should differ and cannot all use four gui with base; color should favor red.'
translations.idiomatic: In Qingli 3 (1043), ritual official Yu Jing said: 'Prayer for grain and sacrifice to the Life-Generating Thearch fall on the same day; their rites should differ and cannot all use four gui with base, with red as the favored color.'

sentences.zh: 乃定祈穀、明堂蒼璧尺二寸，感生帝四圭有邸，朝日日圭、夕月月圭皆五寸，從祀神州無玉，報社稷兩圭有邸，祈不用玉。

translations.literal: Thereupon it was fixed: prayer for grain and Bright Hall use azure bi one foot two inches; Life-Generating Thearch four gui with base; morning sun sun-gui and evening moon moon-gui all five inches; accompanying sacrifice to the Divine Land has no jade; reporting to soil and grain two gui with base; prayer uses no jade.
translations.idiomatic: It was then determined: prayer for grain and the Bright Hall use an azure bi of one foot two inches; the Life-Generating Thearch four gui with base; morning sun and evening moon gui of five inches each; the accompanying sacrifice to the Divine Land has no jade; reporting to soil and grain uses two gui with base; and prayer offerings use no jade.

sentences.zh: 明年，《祀儀》成，比《通禮》多所更定雲。

translations.literal: The next year the Sacrificial Protocols was completed, differing in many respects from the Comprehensive Rites.
translations.idiomatic: The following year the Sacrificial Protocols was completed, with many revisions from the Comprehensive Rites.

sentences.zh: 嘉祐中，集賢校理江休復言：「《六典》大祀養牲，在滌三月，袷享日近，已逾其期，而牲牢未供。

translations.literal: In Jiayou, Academician collator Jiang Xiufu said: 'The Six Institutions state that for great sacrifices victims are nurtured in the pen for three months; the joint offering day is near and the period is already exceeded, yet victims are not supplied.
translations.idiomatic: In Jiayou, Academician collator Jiang Xiufu said: 'The Six Institutions require that victims for great sacrifices be kept in the pen for three months; the joint offering is near and the period has passed, yet victims have not been supplied.

sentences.zh: 乞依漢、唐置廩犧局。」

translations.literal: I beg that a Victim Stables Bureau be established as in Han and Tang.'
translations.idiomatic: He requested that a Victim Stables Bureau be established as in Han and Tang.'

sentences.zh: 下禮院議：歲大小祀幾百數，而牲盛之事，儲養無素，宜如休復言。

translations.literal: The matter was referred to the Ritual Court: each year there are several hundred great and minor sacrifices, yet victim rearing is not prepared in advance; Xiufu's proposal should be adopted.
translations.idiomatic: The Ritual Court deliberated: each year there are several hundred great and minor sacrifices, yet victims are not prepared in advance; Xiufu's proposal should be adopted.

sentences.zh: 乃置廩犧局，設牢預養，籍田舊地，種植粢盛，納於神倉，以待祭祀之用。

translations.literal: A Victim Stables Bureau was established, pens set up for advance rearing; on old ceremonial-field land grain was planted, stored in the spirit granary, and kept for sacrificial use.
translations.idiomatic: A Victim Stables Bureau was established with pens for advance rearing; grain was planted on the old ceremonial fields, stored in the spirit granary, and reserved for sacrifices.

sentences.zh: 元豐六年，詳定禮文所言：「本朝昊天上帝、皇地祇、太祖位各設三牲，非尚質貴誠之義。

translations.literal: In the sixth year of Yuanfeng, the detailed ritual text stated: 'In this dynasty August Heaven, August Earth, and Taizu each have three victims set out—not the meaning of valuing simplicity and sincerity.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth year of Yuanfeng (1083), the detailed ritual text stated: 'In our dynasty August Heaven, August Earth, and Taizu each receive three victims—not the principle of valuing simplicity and sincerity.

sentences.zh: 請親祠圜丘、方澤正配位皆用犢，不設羊豕俎及鼎匕，有司攝事亦如之。

translations.literal: It is requested that at personal sacrifice at the Circular Mound and Square Pond the principal correlate positions all use calves, without sheep and pig trays or tripod ladles; surrogates should do likewise.
translations.idiomatic: It was requested that when the emperor personally sacrifices at the Circular Mound and Square Pond, principal correlate positions use only calves, without sheep and pig trays or tripod ladles; surrogates should follow the same rule.

sentences.zh: 又簠、簋、尊、豆皆非陶器，及用龍杓。

translations.literal: Moreover, fu, gui, zun, and dou are not pottery, and a dragon ladle is used.
translations.idiomatic: Moreover, fu, gui, zun, and dou vessels are not pottery, and a dragon ladle is used.

sentences.zh: 請改用陶，以椫為杓。

translations.literal: It is requested to change to pottery and use birch for the ladle.
translations.idiomatic: It was requested to use pottery instead and birch for the ladles.

sentences.zh: 又請南北郊先行升煙瘞血之禮，至薦奠畢，即如舊儀，於壇坎燔瘞牲幣。

translations.literal: It is also requested that at northern and southern suburbs the rites of raising smoke and burying blood be performed first; when offerings are complete, follow the old protocol of burning and burying victims and silks in the altar pit.
translations.idiomatic: It was also requested that at the northern and southern suburbs the rites of raising smoke and burying blood precede the offerings; when presentation is complete, victims and silks should be burned and buried in the altar pit as before.

sentences.zh: 又北郊皇地祇及神州地祇，當為坎瘞，今乃建壇燔燎，非是。

translations.literal: Moreover, at the northern suburb August Earth and the Earth of the Divine Land should be buried in pits; now altars are built and burned—this is incorrect.
translations.idiomatic: Moreover, at the northern suburb August Earth and the Earth of the Divine Land should be buried in pits; building altars and burning offerings there is incorrect.

sentences.zh: 請今祭地祝版、牲幣並瘞於坎。

translations.literal: It is requested that for earth sacrifices prayer boards, victims, and silks all be buried in pits.
translations.idiomatic: It was requested that for earth sacrifices prayer boards, victims, and silks all be buried in pits.

sentences.zh: 又《祀儀》：惟昊天上帝、皇地祇、高禖燔瘞犢首，自感生帝、神州地祇而下皆不燔瘞牲體，殊不應典禮。

translations.literal: Moreover, the Sacrificial Protocols: only August Heaven, August Earth, and the High Mei burn and bury calf heads; from the Life-Generating Thearch and Earth of the Divine Land downward no victim bodies are burned or buried—this greatly fails to accord with canonical ritual.
translations.idiomatic: Moreover, the Sacrificial Protocols provide that only August Heaven, August Earth, and the High Mei burn and bury calf heads; from the Life-Generating Thearch and Earth of the Divine Land downward no victim bodies are burned or buried—this greatly departs from canonical ritual.

sentences.zh: 請自今昊天上帝、感生帝皆燔牲首以報陽；

translations.literal: From now on let August Heaven and the Life-Generating Thearch all burn victim heads to report to yang;
translations.idiomatic: Henceforth August Heaven and the Life-Generating Thearch should burn victim heads to report to yang;

sentences.zh: 皇地祇、神州、太社、太稷，凡地之祭，皆瘞牲之左髀以報陰。

translations.literal: August Earth, the Divine Land, Grand Altars of Soil and Grain—for all earth sacrifices bury the left thigh of the victim to report to yin.
translations.idiomatic: August Earth, the Divine Land, and the Grand Altars of Soil and Grain—for all earth sacrifices the left thigh of the victim should be buried to report to yin.

sentences.zh: 薦享太廟亦皆升首於室。」

translations.literal: Offerings at the Grand Temple should also all raise the head in the chamber.'
translations.idiomatic: Offerings at the Grand Temple should also raise the head in the inner chamber.'

sentences.zh: 又言：「古者祭祀用牲，有豚解，有體解，薦腥則解為十一體。

translations.literal: He also said: 'In antiquity sacrifices used victims; there was pig dismemberment and body dismemberment; for presenting raw meat the dismemberment was into eleven parts.
translations.idiomatic: He also said: 'In antiquity sacrifices used victims with pig dismemberment or body dismemberment; raw offerings were divided into eleven parts.

sentences.zh: 今親祠南郊，正配位之俎，不殊左右胖，不分貴賤，無豚解、體解之別。

translations.literal: Now at personal sacrifice at the southern suburb, the trays of the principal correlate positions do not distinguish left and right sides, do not separate noble and humble, and have no distinction of pig or body dismemberment.
